A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multilingual hallucination study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including v3's additional prompt tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations, hallucination-rate estimates for 11 LLMs across 30 languages, human annotations, and manual response analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including detector scores in Tables 3 and 10, rate estimates in Figure 4, and manual analysis in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: The QLoRA-trained Llama-3-8B detectors, bidirectional contextualization, token-classification objectives, and precision/recall-adjusted rate estimator are unchanged. The added synthesis prompts document the existing procedure without establishing a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FAVA-based training data, 30 languages, five human-annotated language portions, binary/category detection tasks, and Wikipedia-grounded QA corpus of 25,685 articles and 51,133 queries.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same MONO/MULTI and bidirectional/causal comparisons. The hallucination-rate study retains the same 11 LLMs from six families; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Reported splits, sample sizes, metrics, article filters, training configurations, and generation settings remain unchanged, including the 70:30 training/validation split and 1,024-token generation limit. The newly printed prompts disclose details without establishing revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same gold/silver validation, model-size and language-support comparisons, response-length correlations, and 60-response German/Arabic manual analysis. The latter already appears in v1 Appendix A.7.

E5.justification: The three detector-training seeds, five generation seeds, mean and standard-deviation reporting, Pearson correlations, and Student's t-tests are unchanged. v3 introduces no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and result figures retain their values and findings. Examples include the gold/silver correlation of r = 0.83 and Appendix A.7's 10% repetitive responses and 5% 'I don't know' responses; no new empirical result entries appear.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the precision/recall adjustment derivation are unchanged. The paragraph added after Equation 7 restates the existing false-positive/false-negative rationale without introducing a new formal assumption, result, or proof.

C1.justification: The rewritten abstract and contribution list foreground silver/gold validation, the synthetic QA corpus, and the language-support trend, all already presented in v1. The main contribution scope and conclusions remain the same.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an explanation linking token-level agreement to inconsistencies in minimal-span selection. The limitations qualify confidence in query grounding especially for high-resource languages and drop the explicit statement that multilingual factual-coverage resources are lacking. The synthetic-hallucination realism caveat largely repeats v1 Section 3.1.

D1.justification: v3 Tables 11–17 newly supply the seed-passage generation prompt and all six category-specific hallucination-insertion prompts, including language instructions, tagging rules, and examples. This substantially expands reproducibility documentation for the central data-synthesis process, beyond v1's query-generation prompt and human annotation instructions. v3 also identifies the JURECA computing facility.

R1.justification: v3 removes Chen et al. (2023), 'Beyond factuality,' and adds the JURECA computing-facility reference. Other citation occurrences are trimmed, while the substantive related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract and contribution list, expands explanatory prose, reformats the limitations into paragraphs, and adds acknowledgments while retaining the section organization. Editing is uneven: the final limitations sentence now ends unfinished.

P2.justification: v3 adds seven boxed prompt tables and adjusts appendix float placement and spacing. The original figures retain their graphical content, and the quantitative tables preserve their structures; the visual expansion is concentrated in supplementary documentation.

improvement.justification: Tables 11–17 provide materially better information for auditing and reproducing the existing dataset construction, while the scientific evidence remains unchanged. This documentation benefit outweighs limited editorial regressions, including Section 4.1's incorrect pointer to Table 11 instead of the retained query-generation Table 6 and the unfinished limitations sentence.
